new_findings.what: The launch failure is NOT a model/vLLM gap. The model (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration / qwen3_5_moe, hybrid 30 linear-attn + 10 full-attn, 256-expert MoE) is natively supported by vLLM 0.28.0+rocm723 and resolves at runtime. There are THREE stacked harness-layer blockers in Magpie's benchmark CHILD ENV, all now localized and the first three cleared: (B1, attempt-1, still live in tree) no gfx90a runner type in image_selector; (B2) host-physical HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 vs the ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 GPU lease; (B3) the session-injected PATH=/opt/venv/bin:... which contains no vllm/hf/transformers.

new_findings.expected_impact: Mandatory: without it no server ever initialises, so the baseline and every downstream proposal measure nothing.
new_findings.source: scratch/gpuprobe runs + scratch/neg2/server.log:54,78 + /opt/envs/vllm/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/platforms/rocm.py:128-158 + Magpie/modes/benchmark/benchmarker.py:776,800 (env=os.environ.copy() then benchmark.envs applied verbatim)
new_findings.what: B2 mechanism (this attempt's primary find): ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES filters at the HSA layer AND renumbers the surviving agents to 0..N-1. HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES is applied on top of that already-remapped list, so a host-physical HIP pin (2,3) with ROCR=0,1 selects NOTHING. torch.cuda.device_count() still reports 2 (from ROCR's count) while every allocation dies with 'RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available', and vLLM's worker startup surfaces it as 'Engine core initialization failed'. Reproduced both ways: isolation probe (HIP=2,3+ROCR=0,1 -> FAIL; HIP=0,1 or unset -> 2x MI250X gfx90a + matmul OK) and negative control NEG-2 (ORIGINAL Magpie script + a healthy PATH + HIP=2,3/ROCR=0,1 -> rc=1, worker RuntimeError at scratch/neg2/server.log:54). vllm/platforms/rocm.py:_sync_hip_cuda_env_vars only cross-checks HIP vs CUDA and cannot see this because ROCR is a different layer.

new_findings.expected_impact: Unblocks both the server phase and the throughput client phase.
new_findings.source: scratch/neg1/out.log:28 + probe: env -i PATH=<baseline PATH> -> 'vllm MISSING', python3=/opt/venv/bin/python3, import vllm -> ModuleNotFoundError; and InferenceX/utils/bench_serving/benchmark_serving.py --help failing under unpatched PATH vs succeeding with /opt/envs/vllm/bin prepended
new_findings.what: B3 mechanism (independent, and the failure that appears immediately behind B2): the InferenceX/Magpie vllm_mi300x.sh launches 'setsid vllm serve' and runs the serving client with a bare 'python3'. The session YAML injects PATH=/opt/venv/bin:/usr/local/sbin:...:/bin, but /opt/venv has no vllm, no hf and no transformers, so the server phase dies in ~2s with 'setsid: failed to execute vllm: No such file or directory' (NEG-1, rc=1) and the client phase dies on 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named huggingface_hub'. Magpie itself runs from /opt/envs/vllm/bin/python3, i.e. the correct framework env was known at runtime but never propagated to the child.

new_findings.expected_impact: Raises the combo from non-runnable (0.0 tok/s baseline, 8 denied coordinator rounds) to measurably serving; unblocks the baseline gate.
new_findings.what: DELIVERABLE VERIFIED END-TO-END: with patch 003 applied (i.e. the two new Magpie helpers repairing the child env), the real serving path ran on my leased cards — TP2 + expert-parallel vLLM 0.28.0 on 2x MI250X booted ('Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration', CUDA-graph capture complete, /health 200), generated correct text ('The capital of France is' -> ' Paris.', 16 tok in 2.3s), and completed a full Magpie/InferenceX benchmark_serving run: 64/64 successful requests, 56.9s, output 1151.77 tok/s, total 2303.54 tok/s, mean TTFT 4358.9ms, mean TPOT 50.3ms at concurrency 64 with ISL/OSL 1024/1024 and max_model_len 6144. These are MY validation numbers on my cards for the runnability gate, NOT the sealed baseline (the coordinator owns that measurement).

The durable place is the Magpie package. Script selection is deterministic here: priority-2 native 'benchmarks/gptoss_bf16_mi300x.sh' does not exist, so priority 3 selects the (patched) Magpie generic vllm_mi300x.sh. new_findings.what: Residual RISK (not a code gap, and not fixed by patch 003): the baseline config sets RUN_EVAL=true, vllm_mi300x.sh does 'run_eval ... || exit $?' so an eval-phase failure fails the whole run even after throughput already succeeded, and lm_eval is NOT importable in /opt/envs/vllm. InferenceX's _install_lm_eval_deps() cannot fetch it on this host right now: pip fails against both mirrors.aliyun.com and pypi.org with 'Connection broken: IncompleteRead/BrokenPipe/ConnectionReset', and the stale mirror additionally reports ResolutionImpossible for the 'api' extra. The harness installs it itself (pip install --break-system-packages 'lm-eval[api]' then a pinned --no-deps force-reinstall of EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness@b315ef3b), so a reachable index is the only requirement.

new_findings.expected_impact: Points the explore/static_recon rounds at the levers that actually apply to this host.
new_findings.what: Perf-lever map for whoever follows (enablement is done, so this is hand-off, not this round's deliverable): AITER is hard-gated off on gfx90a in this build (vllm/_aiter_ops.py:134-155 returns get_cdna_version() > 2, i.e. CDNA3+ only), so VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 is a no-op on MI250X — confirmed live: 'Final IR op priority ... rms_norm=[native]'. In-tree MI250X paths DO exist and are env-gated: vllm/model_executor/layers/mi250_kernels.py (MI250_GATE_GEMV) and vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_splitkv_pa.py (VLLM_ROCM_SPLITKV_PA). Also observed: 'Config file not found at vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/E=128,N=512,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI250X_MI250.json' -> MoE is running on default (untuned) configs, and 'Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton'.

residual_questions: Is the gsm8k eval part of the RUNNABILITY gate for this enablement round? If yes, the host needs a reachable PyPI index (or a preinstalled lm-eval): InferenceX auto-installs it inside run_eval, but pip currently fails on both mirrors.aliyun.com and pypi.org with connection resets. Suggested one-time command if the Coordinator has a working egress/proxy: python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --retries 10 'lm-eval[api]'.

Should HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES be removed from the pod/launcher env entirely? Patch 003 repairs it per-child (safe, non-invasive), but the root inconsistency is that the container entrypoint exports host-physical HIP ids while hyperloom pins logical ROCR ids for the lease.

specialist_done.summary: Made Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B + vLLM RUNNABLE, attacking a different (deeper) layer than the reverted attempt-1 patch. Attempt 1's gfx90a->mi300x runner alias is still live in the tree, so the real remaining blockers were two stacked Magpie CHILD-ENV bugs: (B2) the pod exports host-physical HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 while the lease pins ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 — ROCR filters and renumbers at HSA, so HIP selects nothing -> 'RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available' / 'Engine core initialization failed'; (B3) the injected PATH (/opt/venv/bin, no vllm/hf/transformers) -> 'setsid: failed to execute vllm: No such file or directory'. Each was proven independently fatal by negative control against the ORIGINAL scripts (scratch/neg1 rc=1 in ~2s, scratch/neg2 rc=1 worker RuntimeError). Patch 003 adds align_rocm_visible_devices() + ensure_framework_env_on_path() at _build_local_command, the single funnel every local server/client phase passes through, and hardens Magpie/scripts/benchmark/vllm_mi300x.sh, whose existing logic only repinned HIP when HIP was UNSET and so could never repair an already-set physical id. Verified on my cards: real TP2/EP vLLM server booted, CUDA graphs captured, /health 200, correct text generation, and a full Magpie/InferenceX benchmark_serving run completed 64/64 requests at 1151.77 tok/s output (TTFT 4358.9ms, TPOT 50.3ms) — my runnability numbers, not the sealed baseline. Cleared failure: child sees 0 usable GPUs + framework CLI missing. Next (deeper) failure: the eval stage only — lm_eval is not installed and pip cannot reach an index from this host; throughput gate is unaffected. GPU/cards left clean, no processes of mine running.
